summary: The study investigates the ALD growth of TiO2, Ta2O5, and Nb2O5 using metal ethoxides and water as precursors. The reaction mechanisms were analyzed using in situ mass spectrometry, focusing on the behavior of the precursors and the role of temperature in the decomposition and surface reactions. The growth rate and surface reactions were found to be significantly influenced by temperature, with decomposition starting above 300 °C.
evidence: The amounts of the reaction product CH3CH2OD+ (m/z) 47) and its main fragment CH2OD+ (m/z) 32) increased up to about 300 °C where all the metal precursors started to thermally decompose. At 325 °C the ALD growth of Ta2O5 and Nb2O5 can mainly be described as an alternate release of (C2H5)2O during the Ta(OC2H5)5 or Nb(OC2H5)5 pulses and C2H5OD during the D2O pulse.
